fm.pat.common.patchName.label: PATCH NAME
fm.pat.common.patchName.help: Patch name. Allowed characters: space ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + , - . / 0-9 : ; < = > ? @ A-Z [ \ ] ^ _ ` a-z { | } ~ (EM p.5). Values: 12 characters (ASCII 32–127).

fm.pat.common.patchCategory.label: Patch Category
fm.pat.common.patchCategory.help: Category number of the patch (used by the Editor's patch list). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.common.patchPan.label: PAN
fm.pat.common.patchPan.help: Left/right position of the patch. Values: L64–0–63R.

fm.pat.common.patchPriority.label: PRIORITY
fm.pat.common.patchPriority.help: How notes are managed when maximum polyphony (128 voices) is exceeded. LAST: the last-played voices get priority (notes are turned off beginning with the first-played). LOUDEST: the loudest voices get priority (the lowest-volume voice is turned off first). Usually LAST. Values: LAST, LOUDEST.

enumLong.text: the last-played voices get priority (notes are turned off beginning with the first-played)
the loudest voices get priority (the lowest-volume voice is turned off first)

fm.pat.common.patchCoarseTune.label: TUNE COARSE
fm.pat.common.patchCoarseTune.help: Pitch of the patch's sound in semitones (±4 octaves). Values: -48–+48.

fm.pat.common.patchFineTune.label: TUNE FINE
fm.pat.common.patchFineTune.help: Pitch of the patch's sound in 1-cent steps (1 cent = 1/100 semitone). Values: -50–+50.

fm.pat.common.octaveShift.label: OCTAVE SHIFT
fm.pat.common.octaveShift.help: Pitch of the patch's sound in octaves. Values: -3–+3.

fm.pat.common.stretchTuneDepth.label: STRETCH TUNE DEPTH
fm.pat.common.stretchTuneDepth.help: Stretched tuning, the way acoustic pianos are normally tuned: the low range lower and the high range higher than mathematical tuning. OFF: equal temperament. 1–3: higher settings give a greater pitch difference between low and high ranges. Values: OFF, 1–3.

fm.pat.common.analogFeel.label: ANALOG FEEL
fm.pat.common.analogFeel.help: Depth of 1/f modulation (a pleasant, naturally occurring modulation ratio, like a babbling brook or rustling wind). Simulates the natural instability of an analog synthesizer. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.common.monoPoly.label: MONO/POLY
fm.pat.common.monoPoly.help: MONO: only the last-played note sounds; effective for solo instrument patches such as sax or flute. POLY: two or more notes can be played simultaneously. Values: MONO, POLY.

enumLong.text: two or more notes can be played simultaneously

fm.pat.common.legatoSwitch.label: LEGATO SW (Switch)
fm.pat.common.legatoSwitch.help: Whether the Legato Switch is used. Valid only with MONO. When ON, pressing a key while still holding a previous key changes the pitch to the newest key while the note keeps sounding: a smooth transition that simulates a guitarist's hammer-on/pull-off. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.common.legatoRetrigger.label: LEGATO RETRIGGER
fm.pat.common.legatoRetrigger.help: Whether sounds are replayed (ON) or not (OFF) when playing legato. Valid when MONO and LEGATO SW ON. Normally ON. When OFF, holding one key and pressing another changes only the pitch, without playing the new key's attack; set OFF for wind and string phrases or when using modulation with a mono synth keyboard sound. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.common.portamentoSwitch.label: PORTAMENTO SW
fm.pat.common.portamentoSwitch.help: Whether the portamento effect is applied. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.common.portamentoMode.label: PORTAMENTO MODE
fm.pat.common.portamentoMode.help: NORMAL: portamento is always applied. LEGATO: portamento is applied only when you play legato. Values: NORMAL, LEGATO.

enumLong.text: portamento is applied only when you play legato

fm.pat.common.portamentoType.label: PORTAMENTO TYPE
fm.pat.common.portamentoType.help: RATE: uniform speed of pitch change (the time taken corresponds to the pitch distance). TIME: constant time regardless of how far apart the notes are. Values: RATE, TIME.

enumLong.text: uniform speed of pitch change (the time taken corresponds to the pitch distance)
constant time regardless of how far apart the notes are

fm.pat.common.portamentoStart.label: PORTAMENTO START
fm.pat.common.portamentoStart.help: PITCH: a new portamento starts from the current (moving) pitch when another key is pressed during a glide. NOTE: the new portamento begins from the pitch where the current change would have ended. Values: PITCH, NOTE.

enumLong.text: a new portamento starts from the current (moving) pitch when another key is pressed during a glide
the new portamento begins from the pitch where the current change would have ended

fm.pat.common.portamentoTime.label: PORTAMENTO TIME
fm.pat.common.portamentoTime.help: Time over which the pitch changes. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.common.cutoffOffset.label: OFFSET CUTOFF
fm.pat.common.cutoffOffset.help: Offset applied to the tones' TVF CUTOFF. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.resonanceOffset.label: OFFSET RES (Resonance)
fm.pat.common.resonanceOffset.help: Offset applied to the tones' TVF RES (resonance). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.attackTimeOffset.label: OFFSET ATTACK TIME
fm.pat.common.attackTimeOffset.help: Offset applied to TVF Envelope Time 1 and TVA Envelope Time 1 (attack). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.releaseTimeOffset.label: OFFSET RELEASE TIME
fm.pat.common.releaseTimeOffset.help: Offset applied to TVF Envelope Time 4 and TVA Envelope Time 4 (release). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.velocitySensOffset.label: OFFSET VELOCITY SENS
fm.pat.common.velocitySensOffset.help: Offset applied to TVF Cutoff Velocity Sens and TVA VEL SENS (velocity sensitivity). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.patchOutputAssign.label: OUTPUT ASSIGN (PATCH OUTPUT ASSIGN)
fm.pat.common.patchOutputAssign.help: How the direct (unprocessed) sound of the patch is output. MFX: in stereo through the multi-effect (chorus and reverb can also be applied after it). L+R: in stereo to the OUTPUT jacks without passing through the MFX. L: in mono to OUTPUT L without the MFX. R: in mono to OUTPUT R without the MFX. TONE: according to each tone's own OUTPUT ASSIGN. Values: MFX, L+R, L, R, TONE.

enumLong.text: in stereo through the multi-effect (chorus and reverb can also be applied after it)
in stereo to the OUTPUT jacks without passing through the MFX
in mono to OUTPUT L without the MFX
in mono to OUTPUT R without the MFX
according to each tone's own OUTPUT ASSIGN

fm.pat.common.tmtControlSwitch.label: TMT CONTROL SW
fm.pat.common.tmtControlSwitch.help: Use the Matrix Control (destination TMT) to enable (ON) or disable (OFF) sounding of different tones. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.common.pitchBendRangeUp.label: PITCH BEND RANGE UP
fm.pat.common.pitchBendRangeUp.help: Pitch change in semitones when the touch controller is all the way right. Values: 0–+48.

fm.pat.common.pitchBendRangeDown.label: PITCH BEND RANGE DOWN
fm.pat.common.pitchBendRangeDown.help: Pitch change in semitones when the touch controller is all the way left. Values: -48–0.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Source.label: SOURCE 1
fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Source.help: Message used to change tone parameters. OFF: not used. CC01–31, 33–95: controller numbers. PITCH BEND. AFTERTOUCH. VELOCITY: how hard the key is pressed. KEYFOLLOW: keyboard position with C4 = 0. LFO1, LFO2, PITCH ENV, TVF ENV, TVA ENV: internal modulators. Values: OFF, CC01–31, CC33–95, PITCH BEND, AFTERTOUCH, VELOCITY, KEYFOLLOW, LFO1, LFO2, PITCH ENV, TVF ENV, TVA ENV.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Destination1.label: DESTINATION 1-1
fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Destination1.help: Tone parameters controlled by the matrix control; up to four per matrix control, controlled simultaneously. MFX-CTRL1–4 route to the multi-effect control parameters. TMT switches tones (with TMT CONTROL SW ON). Values: OFF, PITCH, CUTOFF, RESONANCE, LEVEL, PAN, OUTPUT LEVEL, CHORUS SEND, REVERB SEND, LFO1/2 PCH DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVF DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVA DEPTH, LFO1/2 PAN DEPTH, LFO1/2 RATE, PCH ENV A-TIME, PCH ENV D-TIME, PCH ENV R-TIME, TVF ENV A-TIME, TVF ENV D-TIME, TVF ENV R-TIME, TVA ENV A-TIME, TVA ENV D-TIME, TVA ENV R-TIME, TMT, FXM DEPTH, MFX-CTRL1–4.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Sens1.label: SENS 1-1
fm.pat.common.matrixControl1Sens1.help: Amount of the matrix control's effect. Positive: modifies the destination in the positive direction (higher, to the right, faster,..) from its current setting; negative: in the negative direction. Larger absolute values = more change; 0 = no effect. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Destination3.help: Tone parameters controlled by the matrix control; up to four per matrix control, controlled simultaneously. MFX-CTRL1–4 route to the multi-effect control parameters. TMT switches tones (with TMT CONTROL SW ON). Values: OFF, PITCH, CUTOFF, RESONANCE, LEVEL, PAN, OUTPUT LEVEL, CHORUS SEND, REVERB SEND, LFO1/2 PCH DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVF DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVA DEPTH, LFO1/2 PAN DEPTH, LFO1/2 RATE, PCH ENV A-TIME, PCH ENV D-TIME, PCH ENV R-TIME, TVF ENV A-TIME, TVF ENV D-TIME, TVF ENV R-TIME, TVA ENV A-TIME, TVA ENV D-TIME, TVA ENV R-TIME, TMT, FXM DEPTH, MFX-CTRL1–4.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Sens3.label: SENS 4-3
fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Sens3.help: Amount of the matrix control's effect. Positive: modifies the destination in the positive direction (higher, to the right, faster,..) from its current setting; negative: in the negative direction. Larger absolute values = more change; 0 = no effect. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Destination4.label: DESTINATION 4-4
fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Destination4.help: Tone parameters controlled by the matrix control; up to four per matrix control, controlled simultaneously. MFX-CTRL1–4 route to the multi-effect control parameters. TMT switches tones (with TMT CONTROL SW ON). Values: OFF, PITCH, CUTOFF, RESONANCE, LEVEL, PAN, OUTPUT LEVEL, CHORUS SEND, REVERB SEND, LFO1/2 PCH DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVF DEPTH, LFO1/2 TVA DEPTH, LFO1/2 PAN DEPTH, LFO1/2 RATE, PCH ENV A-TIME, PCH ENV D-TIME, PCH ENV R-TIME, TVF ENV A-TIME, TVF ENV D-TIME, TVF ENV R-TIME, TVA ENV A-TIME, TVA ENV D-TIME, TVA ENV R-TIME, TMT, FXM DEPTH, MFX-CTRL1–4.

fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Sens4.label: SENS 4-4
fm.pat.common.matrixControl4Sens4.help: Amount of the matrix control's effect. Positive: modifies the destination in the positive direction (higher, to the right, faster,..) from its current setting; negative: in the negative direction. Larger absolute values = more change; 0 = no effect. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxType.label: MFX TYPE
fm.pat.mfx.mfxType.help: Type of multi-effect. 00 THROUGH = no multi-effect. Values: 00: THROUGH – 78: SYMPATHETIC RESONANCE.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxDrySendLevel.label: MFX OUTPUT LEVEL (SEND LEVEL OUT)
fm.pat.mfx.mfxDrySendLevel.help: Volume of the sound processed by the multi-effect. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxChorusSendLevel.label: MFX CHORUS SEND LEVEL (CHO)
fm.pat.mfx.mfxChorusSendLevel.help: Amount of chorus applied to the sound processed by the multi-effect. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxReverbSendLevel.label: MFX REVERB SEND LEVEL (REV)
fm.pat.mfx.mfxReverbSendLevel.help: Amount of reverb applied to the sound processed by the multi-effect. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxOutputAssign.label: MFX Output Assign
fm.pat.mfx.mfxOutputAssign.help: Output of the multi-effect. Only 'A' exists; the MIDI Implementation marks it as ignored on reception. Values: A, ---, ---, ---.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl1Sens.label: SENS 1
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl1Sens.help: Depth of multi-effect control. Positive changes the destination in the positive direction (larger, toward the right, faster,..), negative in the negative direction; larger values give more control. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl2Source.label: CONTROL SOURCE 2
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl2Source.help: MIDI message that controls the corresponding MFX control parameter. OFF: not used. Values: OFF, CC01–31, CC33–95, PITCH BEND, AFTERTOUCH.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl2Sens.label: SENS 2
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl2Sens.help: Depth of multi-effect control. Positive changes the destination in the positive direction (larger, toward the right, faster,..), negative in the negative direction; larger values give more control. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl3Source.label: CONTROL SOURCE 3
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl3Source.help: MIDI message that controls the corresponding MFX control parameter. OFF: not used. Values: OFF, CC01–31, CC33–95, PITCH BEND, AFTERTOUCH.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl3Sens.label: SENS 3

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl4Source.label: CONTROL SOURCE 4
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl4Source.help: MIDI message that controls the corresponding MFX control parameter. OFF: not used. Values: OFF, CC01–31, CC33–95, PITCH BEND, AFTERTOUCH.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl4Sens.label: SENS 4
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControl4Sens.help: Depth of multi-effect control. Positive changes the destination in the positive direction (larger, toward the right, faster,..), negative in the negative direction; larger values give more control. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign1.label: DESTINATION 1
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign1.help: Which MFX parameter the CONTROL SOURCE controls. The selectable parameters depend on the MFX type. Values: per MFX type OFF, 1–16.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign2.label: DESTINATION 2
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign2.help: Which MFX parameter the CONTROL SOURCE controls. The selectable parameters depend on the MFX type. Values: per MFX type OFF, 1–16.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign3.label: DESTINATION 3
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign3.help: Which MFX parameter the CONTROL SOURCE controls. The selectable parameters depend on the MFX type. Values: per MFX type OFF, 1–16.

fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign4.label: DESTINATION 4
fm.pat.mfx.mfxControlAssign4.help: Which MFX parameter the CONTROL SOURCE controls. The selectable parameters depend on the MFX type. Values: per MFX type OFF, 1–16.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-loFreq.label: Low Freq
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-loFreq.help: Frequency of the low range. Values: 200, 400 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-loGain.label: Low Gain
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-loGain.help: Gain of the low range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Freq.label: Mid1 Freq
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Freq.help: Frequency of the middle range 1. Values: 200–8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Gain.label: Mid1 Gain
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Gain.help: Gain of the middle range 1. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Q.label: Mid1 Q
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid1Q.help: Width of the middle range 1. A higher Q narrows the range affected. Values: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Freq.label: Mid2 Freq
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Freq.help: Frequency of the middle range 2. Values: 200–8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Gain.label: Mid2 Gain
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Gain.help: Gain of the middle range 2. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Q.label: Mid2 Q
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-mid2Q.help: Width of the middle range 2. A higher Q narrows the range affected. Values: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-hiFreq.label: High Freq
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-hiFreq.help: Frequency of the high range. Values: 2000, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-hiGain.label: High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.equalizer-hiGain.help: Gain of the high range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band1.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band1.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band2.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band2.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band3.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band3.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band4.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band4.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band5.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band5.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band6.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band6.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band7.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band7.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band8.label: Band1 (250 Hz) … Band8 (8000 Hz)
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-band8.help: Gain of each frequency band. Values: -15–+15 dB each; bands 250, 500, 1000, 1250, 2000, 3150, 4000, 8000 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-width.label: Q
fm.pat.mfx.spectrum-width.help: Simultaneously adjusts the width of the adjusted ranges for all frequency bands. Values: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loLevel.label: Boost/Cut Low / Mid / High
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loLevel.help: Boost and cut each of the Low, Middle and High frequency ranges. At -60 dB the range becomes inaudible; 0 dB equals the input level. Values: -60–+4 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midLevel.label: Boost/Cut Low / Mid / High
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midLevel.help: Boost and cut each of the Low, Middle and High frequency ranges. At -60 dB the range becomes inaudible; 0 dB equals the input level. Values: -60–+4 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-hiLevel.label: Boost/Cut Low / Mid / High
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-hiLevel.help: Boost and cut each of the Low, Middle and High frequency ranges. At -60 dB the range becomes inaudible; 0 dB equals the input level. Values: -60–+4 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loApSw.label: Anti Phase Low Sw
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loApSw.help: Turns the Anti-Phase function on/off for the Low range. When on, the counter-channel of the stereo sound is inverted and added to the signal. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loAp.label: Anti Phase Low Level
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-loAp.help: Level of the Anti-Phase function for the Low range. Adjusting it for certain frequencies lends emphasis to specific parts (effective only for a stereo source). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midApSw.label: Anti Phase Mid Sw
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midApSw.help: Anti-Phase on/off for the Middle range (same as for Low). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midAp.label: Anti Phase Mid Level
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-midAp.help: Anti-Phase level for the Middle range (same as for Low). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-boostSw.label: Low Boost Sw
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-boostSw.help: Turns the Low Booster on/off; emphasizes the bottom to create a heavy bass sound. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.isolator-boostLevel.label: Low Boost Level
fm.pat.mfx.isolator-boostLevel.help: Increasing this value gives a heavier low end. Depending on the Isolator and filter settings this effect may be hard to distinguish. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-freq.label: Boost Frequency
fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-freq.help: Center frequency at which the lower range will be boosted. Values: 50–125 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-gain.label: Boost Gain
fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-gain.help: Amount by which the lower range will be boosted. Values: 0–+12 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-width.label: Boost Width
fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-width.help: Width of the lower range that will be boosted. Values: WIDE, MID, NARROW.

fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-eqLo.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-eqLo.help: Gain of the low / high frequency range (2-band EQ). Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-eqHi.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.lowBoost-eqHi.help: Gain of the low / high frequency range (2-band EQ). Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtType.label: Filter Type
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtType.help: Frequency range that passes: LPF below the cutoff; BPF around the cutoff; HPF above the cutoff; NOTCH everything except the region around the cutoff. Values: LPF, BPF, HPF, NOTCH.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtSlope.label: Filter Slope
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtSlope.help: Attenuation per octave: -12 dB gentle, -24 dB steep, -36 dB extremely steep. Values: -12, -24, -36 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtCutoff.label: Filter Cutoff
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtCutoff.help: Cutoff frequency; higher = higher cutoff. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtReso.label: Filter Resonance
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtReso.help: Filter resonance; higher emphasizes the region near the cutoff. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtGain.label: Filter Gain
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-filtGain.help: Amount of boost for the filter output. Values: 0–+12 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-modSw.label: Modulation Sw
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-modSw.help: On/off switch for cyclic change of the cutoff. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-modWave.label: Modulation Wave
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-modWave.help: How the cutoff is modulated: triangle, square, sine, sawtooth upward (SAW1), sawtooth downward (SAW2). Values: TRI, SQR, SIN, SAW1, SAW2.

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-rateSync.label: rateSync
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-rateSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-rateNote.label: rateNote
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-rateNote.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-attack.label: Attack
fm.pat.mfx.superFilter-attack.help: Speed at which the cutoff changes; effective if Modulation Wave is SQR, SAW1 or SAW2. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step05.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step06.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step09.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step10.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step11.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step12.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step13.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step14.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step15.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-step16.help: Cutoff frequency at each step. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-rateSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-rateHz.help: Rate of modulation (sequence speed). Values: 0.05–10.00 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-rateNote.label: rateNote

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-attack.label: Attack

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtType.help: LPF passes below the cutoff; BPF around it; HPF above it; NOTCH everything except the region around it. Values: LPF, BPF, HPF, NOTCH.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtSlope.label: Filter Slope
fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtSlope.help: Attenuation per octave: gentle, steep, extremely steep. Values: -12, -24, -36 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtReso.label: Filter Resonance
fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtReso.help: Filter resonance; higher emphasizes the region near the cutoff. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtGain.label: Filter Gain
fm.pat.mfx.stepFilter-filtGain.help: Amount of boost for the filter output. Values: 0–+12 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-mix.label: Mix
fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-mix.help: Level of the overtones generated by the enhancer. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-eqLo.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-eqLo.help: Gain of the low / high range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-eqHi.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.enhancer-eqHi.help: Gain of the low / high range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-mode.label: Filter Type
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-mode.help: LPF: the wah effect is applied over a wide frequency range. BPF: over a narrow range. Values: LPF, BPF.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-manual.label: Manual
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-manual.help: Center frequency at which the effect is applied. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-peak.label: Peak
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-peak.help: Amount of wah effect around the center frequency; a higher value narrows the affected range (like Q). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-sens.label: Sens
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-sens.help: Sensitivity with which the filter is controlled. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-polarity.label: Polarity
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-polarity.help: Direction the frequency changes when the filter is modulated: UP toward higher, DOWN toward lower. Values: UP, DOWN.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-rateSync.label: rateSync
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-rateSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-rateNote.label: rateNote
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-rateNote.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-phs.label: Phase
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-phs.help: Phase shift between the left and right sounds while the wah is applied. Values: 0–180 deg.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-eqLo.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-eqLo.help: Gain of the low / high range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-eqHi.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.autoWah-eqHi.help: Gain of the low / high range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-driveSw.label: Drive Sw
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-driveSw.help: Turns Drive on/off. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-drv.label: Drive
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-drv.help: Degree of distortion; also changes the volume. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-vowel1.label: Vowel1 / Vowel2
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-vowel1.help: The two vowels the effect switches between. Values: a, e, i, o, u.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-vowel2.label: Vowel1 / Vowel2
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-vowel2.help: The two vowels the effect switches between. Values: a, e, i, o, u.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateSync.label: rateSync
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateHz.label: Rate
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateHz.help: Frequency at which the two vowels switch. Values: 0.05–10.00 Hz.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateNote.label: rateNote
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-rateNote.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-ksSw.label: Input Sync Sw
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-ksSw.help: Whether the LFO switching the vowels is reset by the input signal (ON) or not (OFF). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-ksThre.label: Input Sync Threshold
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-ksThre.help: Volume level at which the reset is applied. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-manual.label: Manual
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-manual.help: Point at which Vowel 1/2 switch: 49 or less = Vowel 1 lasts longer; 50 = equal; 51 or more = Vowel 2 lasts longer. Values: 0–100.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-eqLo.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-eqLo.help: Gain of the low / high frequency range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-eqHi.label: Low Gain / High Gain
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-eqHi.help: Gain of the low / high frequency range. Values: -15–+15 dB.

fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-pan.label: Pan
fm.pat.mfx.humanizer-pan.help: Stereo location of the output. Values: L64–63R.

fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-spType.label: Speaker Type
fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-spType.help: Type of speaker (see notes for cabinet/speaker/mic of each). Values: SMALL 1, SMALL 2, MIDDLE, JC-120, BUILT-IN 1–5, BG STACK 1–2, MS STACK 1–2, METAL STACK, 2-STACK, 3-STACK.

fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-micSetting.label: Mic Setting
fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-micSetting.help: Location of the mic recording the speaker; it becomes more distant in the order 1, 2, 3. Values: 1, 2, 3.

fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-directLevel.label: Direct Level
fm.pat.mfx.speakerSimulator-directLevel.help: Volume of the direct sound. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.mfx.phaser-mode.label: Mode
fm.pat.mfx.phaser-mode.help: Number of stages in the phaser. Values: 4-STAGE, 8-STAGE, 12-STAGE.

fm.pat.cho.chorus-filt.help: OFF: no filter. LPF: cuts above the Cutoff Freq. HPF: cuts below the Cutoff Freq. Values: OFF, LPF, HPF.

fm.pat.cho.chorus-splt.label: Cutoff Freq
fm.pat.cho.chorus-splt.help: Basic frequency of the filter. Values: 200–8000 Hz.

fm.pat.cho.chorus-delay.label: Pre Delay
fm.pat.cho.chorus-delay.help: Delay from the direct sound until the chorus sound is heard. Values: 0.0–100 msec.

fm.pat.cho.chorus-rateSync.label: rateSync
fm.pat.cho.chorus-rateSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.cho.chorus-rateNote.label: rateNote

fm.pat.cho.chorus-phs.label: Phase
fm.pat.cho.chorus-phs.help: Spatial spread of the sound. Values: 0–180 deg.

fm.pat.cho.chorus-fb.label: Feedback
fm.pat.cho.chorus-fb.help: Amount of the chorus sound fed back into the effect. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyLSync.label: dlyLSync

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyLMsec.help: Delay from the direct sound until each delay sound is heard. Values: 0–1000 msec.

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyLNote.label: dlyLNote
fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyLNote.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyRSync.label: dlyRSync
fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyRSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyRMsec.label: Delay Left / Delay Right / Delay Center

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyRNote.label: dlyRNote

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCSync.label: dlyCSync
fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCSync.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCMsec.label: Delay Left / Delay Right / Delay Center
fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCMsec.help: Delay from the direct sound until each delay sound is heard. Values: 0–1000 msec.

fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCNote.label: dlyCNote
fm.pat.cho.delay-dlyCNote.help: Tempo-sync variant; not in the AX-Synth manual (leave at its default).

fm.pat.cho.delay-fbk.label: Center Feedback
fm.pat.cho.delay-fbk.help: Proportion of the delay sound fed back into the effect; negative inverts the phase. Values: -98–+98%.

fm.pat.cho.delay-hfDamp.label: HF Damp
fm.pat.cho.delay-hfDamp.help: Frequency above which the fed-back sound is cut. BYPASS: no cut. Values: 200–8000 Hz, BYPASS.

fm.pat.cho.delay-levelL.label: Left Level / Right Level / Center Level
fm.pat.cho.delay-levelL.help: Volume of each delay sound. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.cho.delay-levelR.label: Left Level / Right Level / Center Level
fm.pat.cho.delay-levelR.help: Volume of each delay sound. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.cho.delay-levelC.label: Left Level / Right Level / Center Level
fm.pat.cho.delay-levelC.help: Volume of each delay sound. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.reverbType.label: REVERB TYPE
fm.pat.rev.reverbType.help: OFF: not used. REVERB: basic reverb (with room/stage/hall and delay variations). SRV ROOM: simulates room reverberation in greater detail. SRV HALL: simulates hall reverberation in greater detail. SRV PLATE: simulation of plate echo (a reverb device using a vibrating metal plate). Values: OFF, REVERB, SRV ROOM, SRV HALL, SRV PLATE.

fm.pat.rev.reverbLevel.label: REVERB LEVEL
fm.pat.rev.reverbLevel.help: Volume of the sound processed by the reverb. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.reverbOutputAssign.label: Reverb Output Assign
fm.pat.rev.reverbOutputAssign.help: Output of the reverb; only 'A' exists; ignored on reception. Values: A, ---, ---, ---.

fm.pat.rev.reverb-type.label: Type
fm.pat.rev.reverb-type.help: ROOM1: short reverb with high density. ROOM2: short reverb with low density. STAGE1: more late reverberation. STAGE2: strong early reflections. HALL1: very clear-sounding reverb. HALL2: rich reverb. DELAY: conventional delay effect. PAN-DELAY: delay with echoes that pan left and right. Values: ROOM1, ROOM2, STAGE1, STAGE2, HALL1, HALL2, DELAY, PAN-DELAY.

fm.pat.rev.reverb-time.label: Time
fm.pat.rev.reverb-time.help: Length of the reverberation (types ROOM1–HALL2) or the delay time (types DELAY, PAN-DELAY). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.reverb-HF.label: HF Damp
fm.pat.rev.reverb-HF.help: Frequency above which the high-frequency content of the reverb sound is cut ('damped'). BYPASS: no cut. Values: 200–8000 Hz, BYPASS.

fm.pat.rev.reverb-fb.label: Delay Feedback
fm.pat.rev.reverb-fb.help: Amount of delay sound returned to the input; valid only when Type is DELAY or PAN-DELAY. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-dly.label: Pre Delay
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-dly.help: Delay from the direct sound until the reverb sound is heard. Values: 0.0–100 msec.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-size.label: Size
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-size.help: Size of the simulated room or hall. Values: 1–8.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-hicut.label: High Cut
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-hicut.help: Frequency above which the high-frequency content of the reverb is reduced. BYPASS: no reduction. Values: 160–12500 Hz, BYPASS.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-dfsn.label: Diffusion
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-dfsn.help: Change in the density of the reverb over time; higher = density increases more with time (most pronounced with long reverb times). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-lfdmpf.label: LF Damp Freq
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-lfdmpf.help: Frequency below which the low-frequency content of the reverb is reduced ('damped'). Values: 50–4000 Hz.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-lfdmpg.label: LF Damp Gain
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-lfdmpg.help: Amount of damping applied below LF Damp Freq; 0 = no reduction of the low frequencies. Values: -36–0 dB.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-HFDmpF.label: HF Damp Freq
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-HFDmpF.help: Frequency above which the high-frequency content of the reverb is reduced ('damped'). Values: 4000–12500 Hz.

fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-HFDmpG.label: HF Damp Gain
fm.pat.rev.srvRoom-HFDmpG.help: Amount of damping applied above HF Damp Freq; 0 = no reduction of the high frequencies. Values: -36–0 dB.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-dly.label: Pre Delay
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-dly.help: Delay from the direct sound until the reverb sound is heard. Values: 0.0–100 msec.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-size.label: Size
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-size.help: Size of the simulated room or hall. Values: 1–8.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-hicut.label: High Cut
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-hicut.help: Frequency above which the high-frequency content is reduced. BYPASS: no reduction. Values: 160–12500 Hz, BYPASS.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-dfsn.label: Diffusion
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-dfsn.help: Change in density over time; higher = density increases more with time. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-lfdmpf.label: LF Damp Freq
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-lfdmpf.help: Frequency below which the low frequencies are damped. Values: 50–4000 Hz.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-lfdmpg.label: LF Damp Gain
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-lfdmpg.help: Amount of low-frequency damping; 0 = none. Values: -36–0 dB.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-HFDmpF.label: HF Damp Freq
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-HFDmpF.help: Frequency above which the high frequencies are damped. Values: 4000–12500 Hz.

fm.pat.rev.srvHall-HFDmpG.label: HF Damp Gain
fm.pat.rev.srvHall-HFDmpG.help: Amount of high-frequency damping; 0 = none. Values: -36–0 dB.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-dly.label: Pre Delay
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-dly.help: Delay from the direct sound until the reverb sound is heard. Values: 0.0–100 msec.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-size.label: Size
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-size.help: Size of the simulated space. Values: 1–8.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-hicut.label: High Cut
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-hicut.help: Frequency above which the high-frequency content is reduced. BYPASS: no reduction. Values: 160–12500 Hz, BYPASS.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-dfsn.label: Diffusion
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-dfsn.help: Change in density over time; higher = density increases more with time. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-lfdmpf.label: LF Damp Freq
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-lfdmpf.help: Frequency below which the low frequencies are damped. Values: 50–4000 Hz.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-lfdmpg.label: LF Damp Gain
fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-lfdmpg.help: Amount of low-frequency damping; 0 = none. Values: -36–0 dB.

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-HFDmpF.label: HF Damp Freq

fm.pat.rev.srvPlate-HFDmpG.label: HF Damp Gain

fm.pat.tmt.structureType12.label: STRUCTURE TONE 1 & 2 TYPE
fm.pat.tmt.structureType12.help: How tones 1 and 2 are connected (independent, stacked filters, booster, ring modulator variants). TYPE 01: tones 1 and 2 (or 3 and 4) are independent. Use it to preserve PCM sounds or to create and combine sounds per tone. Values: TYPE 1–10.

fm.pat.tmt.booster12.label: BOOSTER (TONE 1 & 2)
fm.pat.tmt.booster12.help: Amount of boost applied when the Structure Type is 03 or 04. The booster distorts the sound by boosting the input signal (electric-guitar-style distortion); higher = stronger distortion. Values: 0, +6, +12, +18 (dB).

fm.pat.tmt.structureType34.label: STRUCTURE TONE 3 & 4 TYPE
fm.pat.tmt.structureType34.help: How tones 3 and 4 are connected. TYPE 01: tones 1 and 2 (or 3 and 4) are independent. Use it to preserve PCM sounds or to create and combine sounds per tone. Values: TYPE 1–10.

fm.pat.tmt.booster34.label: BOOSTER (TONE 3 & 4)
fm.pat.tmt.booster34.help: Same as BOOSTER for tones 3 & 4. Values: 0, +6, +12, +18 (dB).

fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityControl.label: VELOCITY CONTROL
fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityControl.help: Whether a different tone is played depending on velocity (ON) or not (OFF). RANDOM: the patch's tones sound randomly regardless of velocity. CYCLE: the tones sound consecutively regardless of velocity. Set OFF when using Matrix Control to switch tones. Values: OFF, ON, RANDOM, CYCLE.

fm.pat.tmt.tmtToneSwitch[0].help: Turns each of the four tones on (heard) or off (silent). Turning off unneeded tones conserves polyphony. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tmt.tmtKeyboardRangeUpper[0].label: KEY RANGE UPPER 1

fm.pat.tmt.tmtKeyboardFadeWidthLower[0].label: KEY FADE LOWER 1
fm.pat.tmt.tmtKeyboardFadeWidthLower[0].help: What happens to the tone's level when a note lower than Key Range Lower is played. Set 0 if the tone should not sound at all. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tmt.tmtKeyboardFadeWidthUpper[0].label: KEY FADE UPPER 1

fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityRangeUpper[0].label: VELOCITY RANGE UPPER 1

fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityFadeWidthLower[0].label: VELOCITY FADE LOWER 1
fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityFadeWidthLower[0].help: What happens to the tone's level when played at a velocity lower than Velocity Range Lower (a fade). Set 0 if the tone should not sound at all below the range. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tmt.tmtVelocityRangeUpper[2].label: VELOCITY RANGE UPPER 3

fm.pat.tone[0].toneLevel.label: LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[0].toneLevel.help: Volume of the tone; mainly for adjusting the volume balance between tones. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneCoarseTune.label: TUNE COARSE
fm.pat.tone[0].toneCoarseTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in semitones (±4 octaves). Values: -48–+48.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneFineTune.label: TUNE FINE
fm.pat.tone[0].toneFineTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in 1-cent steps (1/100 semitone). Values: -50–+50.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneRandomPitchDepth.label: RANDOM PITCH
fm.pat.tone[0].toneRandomPitchDepth.help: Width of random pitch deviation each time a key is pressed. Set 0 for no random pitch change. Values: 0–1200 (cents; stored as 31 steps: 0–10, 20–100 by 10, 200–1200 by 100).

fm.pat.tone[0].tonePan.label: PAN
fm.pat.tone[0].tonePan.help: Left/right position of the tone. Values: L64–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[0].tonePanKeyfollow.label: PAN KF (Pan Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].tonePanKeyfollow.help: Makes key position affect panning: positive = notes above C4 pan increasingly to the right; negative = to the left; larger = more change. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneRandomPanDepth.label: RANDOM PAN DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[0].toneRandomPanDepth.help: Stereo position changes randomly each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. Values: 0–63.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneAlternatePanDepth.label: ALT. PAN DEPTH (Alternate Pan Depth)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneAlternatePanDepth.help: Panning alternates between left and right each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. L or R reverses the alternation order: two tones set to L and R respectively alternate opposite to each other. Values: L63–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneEnvMode.label: ENV MODE (Envelope Mode)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneEnvMode.help: With a loop waveform the sound normally continues while the key is held; NO-SUS makes it decay naturally even with the key held. A one-shot wave does not sustain even with SUSTAIN. Values: NO-SUS, SUSTAIN.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneDelayMode.label: TONE DELAY MODE
fm.pat.tone[0].toneDelayMode.help: NORMAL: the tone begins after the delay time. HOLD: begins after the delay time, but if the key is released before the time has elapsed the tone is not played. KEY-OFF-NOR: the tone begins the delay time after the key is released instead of while it is held (e.g. simulating guitar noises). KEY-OFF-DCY: like KEY-OFF-NOR but the TVA envelope already runs while the key is held, so often only the release portion is heard. With a decaying (one-shot) wave, KEY-OFF modes may give no sound. Values: NORMAL, HOLD, KEY-OFF-NOR, KEY-OFF-DCY.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneDelayTime.label: TONE DELAY TIME
fm.pat.tone[0].toneDelayTime.help: Time from key press (or, in KEY-OFF modes, from key release) until the tone sounds. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneDrySendLevel.label: SEND LEVEL OUT (Output Level / TONE OUTPUT LEVEL)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneDrySendLevel.help: Level of the tone's signal sent to the destination set by OUTPUT ASSIGN. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[0].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[0].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneOutputAssign.label: OUTPUT ASSIGN (TONE OUTPUT ASSIGN)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneOutputAssign.help: How the tone's direct sound is output. MFX: stereo through the multi-effect (chorus/reverb can follow). L+R: stereo to the OUTPUT jacks bypassing the MFX. L / R: mono to OUTPUT L / R bypassing the MFX. Valid only if PATCH OUTPUT ASSIGN is TONE. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: MFX, L+R, L, R.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveBender.label: RCV BENDER (Receive Bender)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveBender.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Pitch Bend. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveExpression.label: RCV EXP (Receive Expression)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveExpression.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Expression (CC11). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveHold-1.label: RCV HOLD-1 (Receive Hold-1)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceiveHold-1.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Hold-1 (CC64). No effect if ENV MODE is NO-SUS. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceivePanMode.label: RCV PAN MODE (Receive Pan Mode)
fm.pat.tone[0].toneReceivePanMode.help: How Pan messages are received. CONTINUOUS: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives. KEY-ON: the pan changes only when the next note is played. Pan messages cannot be ignored entirely. Values: CONTINUOUS, KEY-ON.

enumLong.text: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives
the pan changes only when the next note is played

fm.pat.tone[0].toneRedamperSwitch.label: REDAMPER
fm.pat.tone[0].toneRedamperSwitch.help: Whether the sound is held when Hold 1 is received after a key is released but before the sound has decayed to silence; set ON to sustain. Effective for piano sounds. Requires RCV HOLD-1 ON. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-1
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-2
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-3
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-4
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl1Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-1
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-2
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-3
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-4
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl2Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-1
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-2
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-3
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-4
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl3Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-1
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-2
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-3
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-4
fm.pat.tone[0].toneControl4Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveGroupType.label: Wave Group Type
fm.pat.tone[0].waveGroupType.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveGroupID.label: Wave Group ID
fm.pat.tone[0].waveGroupID.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveNumberL.label: WAVE NUMBER L (Mono)
fm.pat.tone[0].waveNumberL.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveNumberR.label: WAVE NUMBER R
fm.pat.tone[0].waveNumberR.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveGain.label: GAIN
fm.pat.tone[0].waveGain.help: Gain (amplification) of the waveform in 6 dB steps; +6 dB doubles the gain. When using the Booster to distort the sound, set this to its maximum. Values: -6, 0, +6, +12 (dB).

fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMSwitch.label: FXM ON
fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMSwitch.help: Whether FXM (frequency cross modulation) is used. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMColor.label: FXM COLOR
fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMColor.help: How FXM performs frequency modulation: higher settings give a grainier sound, lower settings a more metallic sound. Values: 1–4.

fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMDepth.label: FXM DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[0].waveFXMDepth.help: Depth of the modulation produced by FXM. Values: 0–16.

fm.pat.tone[0].wavePitchKeyfollow.label: PITCH KF (Pitch Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].wavePitchKeyfollow.help: Amount of pitch change when you play a key one octave higher. +100: the pitch rises one octave per octave as on a conventional keyboard; +200: two octaves. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (PITCH ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvDepth.help: Depth of the pitch envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -12–+12.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvVelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics control the pitch envelope depth; positive = more effect for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS (T1 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS (T4 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.help: Makes pitch envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position. Relative to C4, positive settings make notes above C4 have increasingly shorter times. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime1.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime2.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime3.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvTime4.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel0.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel1.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel2.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel3.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[0].pitchEnvLevel4.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfFilterType.label: FILTER TYPE
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfFilterType.help: OFF: no filter. LPF (low pass): reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound. BPF (band pass): leaves only frequencies around the cutoff; useful for distinctive sounds. HPF (high pass): cuts frequencies below the cutoff; suits percussive sounds emphasizing higher tones. PKG (peaking): emphasizes frequencies around the cutoff; with an LFO sweeping the cutoff gives wah-wah. LPF2: low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF; good for simulated instruments such as acoustic piano. LPF3: low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency; also for acoustic instruments, with a different nuance from LPF2 even with the same envelope. With LPF2/LPF3 the RES setting is ignored. Values: OFF, LPF, BPF, HPF, PKG, LPF2, LPF3.

enumLong.text: reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound
leaves only frequencies around the cutoff
low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF
low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffFrequency.label: CUTOFF (Cutoff Frequency)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffFrequency.help: Frequency at which the filter begins to affect the waveform's frequency components. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.label: CUTOFF KF (Cutoff Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.help: Makes the cutoff depend on the key played. Relative to C4, positive settings raise the cutoff for notes above C4, negative settings lower it; larger = more change. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Cutoff Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the cutoff frequency. FIX: the cutoff is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Cutoff Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.help: How playing velocity changes the cutoff; positive = strongly played notes raise the cutoff (brighter). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfResonance.label: RES (Resonance)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfResonance.help: Emphasizes the region around the cutoff frequency, adding character. Excessively high settings can produce oscillation, causing distortion. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.label: RES VEL SENS (Resonance Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.help: Lets velocity modify the resonance amount; positive = strongly played notes get more resonance. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (FILTER ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvDepth.help: Depth of the TVF envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the TVF envelope. FIX: the envelope is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvVelocitySens.help: How velocity affects the TVF envelope depth; positive = greater effect for strongly played notes, negative = less. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 of the TVF envelope; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 of the TVF envelope; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVF envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime1.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime2.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime3.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvTime4.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel0.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel1.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel2.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel3.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[0].tvfEnvLevel4.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].biasLevel.label: BIAS LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[0].biasLevel.help: Bias makes the volume depend on keyboard position (useful for acoustic instruments). BIAS LEVEL is the angle of the volume change in the selected direction; larger = more change; negative inverts the direction. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].biasPosition.label: BIAS POSITION
fm.pat.tone[0].biasPosition.help: Key relative to which the volume is modified. Values: C-1–G9.

fm.pat.tone[0].biasDirection.label: BIAS DIRECTION
fm.pat.tone[0].biasDirection.help: LOWER: volume modified below the bias position. UPPER: above it. LO&UP: symmetrically on both sides. ALL: volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center. Values: LOWER, UPPER, LO&UP, ALL.

enumLong.text: volume modified below the bias position
volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the volume. FIX: the tone's volume is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaLevelVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaLevelVelocitySens.help: How playing dynamics change the tone's volume; positive = louder the harder you play; negative = softer the harder you play. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 (attack) of the TVA envelope; positive = faster for strongly played notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 (release); positive = faster for quickly released notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVA envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes, negative = longer; larger = more change. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime1.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime2.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime3.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvTime4.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel1.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel1.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel2.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel2.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel3.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 3
fm.pat.tone[0].tvaEnvLevel3.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoWaveForm[0].label: WAVEFORM 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoWaveForm[0].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRate[0].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRate[0].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoOffset[0].label: OFFSET 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoOffset[0].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRateDetune[0].label: RATE DETUNE 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRateDetune[0].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTime[0].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTime[0].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeMode[0].label: FADE MODE 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeMode[0].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeTime[0].label: FADE TIME 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeTime[0].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoKeyTrigger[0].label: KEY TRIGGER 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoKeyTrigger[0].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPitchDepth[0].label: DEPTH PITCH 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPitchDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvfDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVF 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvfDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvaDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVA 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvaDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPanDepth[0].label: DEPTH PAN 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPanDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoWaveForm[1].label: WAVEFORM 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoWaveForm[1].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRate[1].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRate[1].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoOffset[1].label: OFFSET 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoOffset[1].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRateDetune[1].label: RATE DETUNE 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoRateDetune[1].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTime[1].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTime[1].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeMode[1].label: FADE MODE 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeMode[1].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeTime[1].label: FADE TIME 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoFadeTime[1].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoKeyTrigger[1].label: KEY TRIGGER 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoKeyTrigger[1].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPitchDepth[1].label: DEPTH PITCH 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPitchDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvfDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVF 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvfDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvaDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVA 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoTvaDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPanDepth[1].label: DEPTH PAN 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoPanDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStepType.label: STEP TYPE
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStepType.help: Whether the step LFO level changes abruptly at each step (TYPE1: stair-step) or is connected linearly (TYPE2: linear). Values: TYPE1, TYPE2.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep1.label: STEP 1–16 1
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep1.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep2.label: STEP 1–16 2
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep2.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep3.label: STEP 1–16 3
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep3.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep4.label: STEP 1–16 4
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep4.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep5.label: STEP 1–16 5
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep5.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep6.label: STEP 1–16 6
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep6.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep7.label: STEP 1–16 7
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep7.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep8.label: STEP 1–16 8
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep8.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep9.label: STEP 1–16 9
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep9.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep10.label: STEP 1–16 10
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep10.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep11.label: STEP 1–16 11
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep11.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep12.label: STEP 1–16 12
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep12.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep13.label: STEP 1–16 13
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep13.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep14.label: STEP 1–16 14
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep14.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep15.label: STEP 1–16 15
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep15.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep16.label: STEP 1–16 16
fm.pat.tone[0].lfoStep16.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneLevel.label: LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[1].toneLevel.help: Volume of the tone; mainly for adjusting the volume balance between tones. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneCoarseTune.label: TUNE COARSE
fm.pat.tone[1].toneCoarseTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in semitones (±4 octaves). Values: -48–+48.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneFineTune.label: TUNE FINE
fm.pat.tone[1].toneFineTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in 1-cent steps (1/100 semitone). Values: -50–+50.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneRandomPitchDepth.label: RANDOM PITCH
fm.pat.tone[1].toneRandomPitchDepth.help: Width of random pitch deviation each time a key is pressed. Set 0 for no random pitch change. Values: 0–1200 (cents; stored as 31 steps: 0–10, 20–100 by 10, 200–1200 by 100).

fm.pat.tone[1].tonePan.label: PAN
fm.pat.tone[1].tonePan.help: Left/right position of the tone. Values: L64–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[1].tonePanKeyfollow.label: PAN KF (Pan Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].tonePanKeyfollow.help: Makes key position affect panning: positive = notes above C4 pan increasingly to the right; negative = to the left; larger = more change. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneRandomPanDepth.label: RANDOM PAN DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[1].toneRandomPanDepth.help: Stereo position changes randomly each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. Values: 0–63.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneAlternatePanDepth.label: ALT. PAN DEPTH (Alternate Pan Depth)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneAlternatePanDepth.help: Panning alternates between left and right each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. L or R reverses the alternation order: two tones set to L and R respectively alternate opposite to each other. Values: L63–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneEnvMode.label: ENV MODE (Envelope Mode)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneEnvMode.help: With a loop waveform the sound normally continues while the key is held; NO-SUS makes it decay naturally even with the key held. A one-shot wave does not sustain even with SUSTAIN. Values: NO-SUS, SUSTAIN.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneDelayMode.label: TONE DELAY MODE
fm.pat.tone[1].toneDelayMode.help: NORMAL: the tone begins after the delay time. HOLD: begins after the delay time, but if the key is released before the time has elapsed the tone is not played. KEY-OFF-NOR: the tone begins the delay time after the key is released instead of while it is held (e.g. simulating guitar noises). KEY-OFF-DCY: like KEY-OFF-NOR but the TVA envelope already runs while the key is held, so often only the release portion is heard. With a decaying (one-shot) wave, KEY-OFF modes may give no sound. Values: NORMAL, HOLD, KEY-OFF-NOR, KEY-OFF-DCY.
