fm.pat.tone[1].toneDelayTime.label: TONE DELAY TIME
fm.pat.tone[1].toneDelayTime.help: Time from key press (or, in KEY-OFF modes, from key release) until the tone sounds. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneDrySendLevel.label: SEND LEVEL OUT (Output Level / TONE OUTPUT LEVEL)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneDrySendLevel.help: Level of the tone's signal sent to the destination set by OUTPUT ASSIGN. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[1].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[1].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneOutputAssign.label: OUTPUT ASSIGN (TONE OUTPUT ASSIGN)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneOutputAssign.help: How the tone's direct sound is output. MFX: stereo through the multi-effect (chorus/reverb can follow). L+R: stereo to the OUTPUT jacks bypassing the MFX. L / R: mono to OUTPUT L / R bypassing the MFX. Valid only if PATCH OUTPUT ASSIGN is TONE. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: MFX, L+R, L, R.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveBender.label: RCV BENDER (Receive Bender)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveBender.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Pitch Bend. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveExpression.label: RCV EXP (Receive Expression)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveExpression.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Expression (CC11). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveHold-1.label: RCV HOLD-1 (Receive Hold-1)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceiveHold-1.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Hold-1 (CC64). No effect if ENV MODE is NO-SUS. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceivePanMode.label: RCV PAN MODE (Receive Pan Mode)
fm.pat.tone[1].toneReceivePanMode.help: How Pan messages are received. CONTINUOUS: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives. KEY-ON: the pan changes only when the next note is played. Pan messages cannot be ignored entirely. Values: CONTINUOUS, KEY-ON.

enumLong.text: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives
the pan changes only when the next note is played

fm.pat.tone[1].toneRedamperSwitch.label: REDAMPER
fm.pat.tone[1].toneRedamperSwitch.help: Whether the sound is held when Hold 1 is received after a key is released but before the sound has decayed to silence; set ON to sustain. Effective for piano sounds. Requires RCV HOLD-1 ON. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-1
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-2
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-3
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-4
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl1Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-1
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-2
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-3
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-4
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl2Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-1
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-2
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-3
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-4
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl3Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-1
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-2
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-3
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-4
fm.pat.tone[1].toneControl4Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveGroupType.label: Wave Group Type
fm.pat.tone[1].waveGroupType.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveGroupID.label: Wave Group ID
fm.pat.tone[1].waveGroupID.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveNumberL.label: WAVE NUMBER L (Mono)
fm.pat.tone[1].waveNumberL.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveNumberR.label: WAVE NUMBER R
fm.pat.tone[1].waveNumberR.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveGain.label: GAIN
fm.pat.tone[1].waveGain.help: Gain (amplification) of the waveform in 6 dB steps; +6 dB doubles the gain. When using the Booster to distort the sound, set this to its maximum. Values: -6, 0, +6, +12 (dB).

fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMSwitch.label: FXM ON
fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMSwitch.help: Whether FXM (frequency cross modulation) is used. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMColor.label: FXM COLOR
fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMColor.help: How FXM performs frequency modulation: higher settings give a grainier sound, lower settings a more metallic sound. Values: 1–4.

fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMDepth.label: FXM DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[1].waveFXMDepth.help: Depth of the modulation produced by FXM. Values: 0–16.

fm.pat.tone[1].wavePitchKeyfollow.label: PITCH KF (Pitch Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].wavePitchKeyfollow.help: Amount of pitch change when you play a key one octave higher. +100: the pitch rises one octave per octave as on a conventional keyboard; +200: two octaves. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (PITCH ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvDepth.help: Depth of the pitch envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -12–+12.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvVelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics control the pitch envelope depth; positive = more effect for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS (T1 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS (T4 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.help: Makes pitch envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position. Relative to C4, positive settings make notes above C4 have increasingly shorter times. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime1.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime2.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime3.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvTime4.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel0.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel1.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel2.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel3.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[1].pitchEnvLevel4.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfFilterType.label: FILTER TYPE
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfFilterType.help: OFF: no filter. LPF (low pass): reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound. BPF (band pass): leaves only frequencies around the cutoff; useful for distinctive sounds. HPF (high pass): cuts frequencies below the cutoff; suits percussive sounds emphasizing higher tones. PKG (peaking): emphasizes frequencies around the cutoff; with an LFO sweeping the cutoff gives wah-wah. LPF2: low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF; good for simulated instruments such as acoustic piano. LPF3: low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency; also for acoustic instruments, with a different nuance from LPF2 even with the same envelope. With LPF2/LPF3 the RES setting is ignored. Values: OFF, LPF, BPF, HPF, PKG, LPF2, LPF3.

enumLong.text: reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound
leaves only frequencies around the cutoff
low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF
low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffFrequency.label: CUTOFF (Cutoff Frequency)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffFrequency.help: Frequency at which the filter begins to affect the waveform's frequency components. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.label: CUTOFF KF (Cutoff Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.help: Makes the cutoff depend on the key played. Relative to C4, positive settings raise the cutoff for notes above C4, negative settings lower it; larger = more change. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Cutoff Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the cutoff frequency. FIX: the cutoff is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Cutoff Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.help: How playing velocity changes the cutoff; positive = strongly played notes raise the cutoff (brighter). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfResonance.label: RES (Resonance)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfResonance.help: Emphasizes the region around the cutoff frequency, adding character. Excessively high settings can produce oscillation, causing distortion. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.label: RES VEL SENS (Resonance Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.help: Lets velocity modify the resonance amount; positive = strongly played notes get more resonance. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (FILTER ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvDepth.help: Depth of the TVF envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the TVF envelope. FIX: the envelope is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvVelocitySens.help: How velocity affects the TVF envelope depth; positive = greater effect for strongly played notes, negative = less. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 of the TVF envelope; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 of the TVF envelope; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVF envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime1.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime2.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime3.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvTime4.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel0.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel1.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel2.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel3.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[1].tvfEnvLevel4.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].biasLevel.label: BIAS LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[1].biasLevel.help: Bias makes the volume depend on keyboard position (useful for acoustic instruments). BIAS LEVEL is the angle of the volume change in the selected direction; larger = more change; negative inverts the direction. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].biasPosition.label: BIAS POSITION
fm.pat.tone[1].biasPosition.help: Key relative to which the volume is modified. Values: C-1–G9.

fm.pat.tone[1].biasDirection.label: BIAS DIRECTION
fm.pat.tone[1].biasDirection.help: LOWER: volume modified below the bias position. UPPER: above it. LO&UP: symmetrically on both sides. ALL: volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center. Values: LOWER, UPPER, LO&UP, ALL.

enumLong.text: volume modified below the bias position
volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the volume. FIX: the tone's volume is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaLevelVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaLevelVelocitySens.help: How playing dynamics change the tone's volume; positive = louder the harder you play; negative = softer the harder you play. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 (attack) of the TVA envelope; positive = faster for strongly played notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 (release); positive = faster for quickly released notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVA envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes, negative = longer; larger = more change. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime1.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime2.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime3.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvTime4.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel1.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel1.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel2.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel2.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel3.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 3
fm.pat.tone[1].tvaEnvLevel3.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoWaveForm[0].label: WAVEFORM 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoWaveForm[0].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRate[0].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRate[0].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoOffset[0].label: OFFSET 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoOffset[0].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRateDetune[0].label: RATE DETUNE 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRateDetune[0].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTime[0].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTime[0].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeMode[0].label: FADE MODE 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeMode[0].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeTime[0].label: FADE TIME 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeTime[0].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoKeyTrigger[0].label: KEY TRIGGER 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoKeyTrigger[0].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPitchDepth[0].label: DEPTH PITCH 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPitchDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvfDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVF 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvfDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvaDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVA 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvaDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPanDepth[0].label: DEPTH PAN 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPanDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoWaveForm[1].label: WAVEFORM 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoWaveForm[1].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRate[1].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRate[1].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoOffset[1].label: OFFSET 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoOffset[1].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRateDetune[1].label: RATE DETUNE 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoRateDetune[1].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTime[1].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTime[1].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeMode[1].label: FADE MODE 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeMode[1].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeTime[1].label: FADE TIME 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoFadeTime[1].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoKeyTrigger[1].label: KEY TRIGGER 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoKeyTrigger[1].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPitchDepth[1].label: DEPTH PITCH 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPitchDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvfDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVF 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvfDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvaDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVA 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoTvaDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPanDepth[1].label: DEPTH PAN 2
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoPanDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStepType.label: STEP TYPE
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStepType.help: Whether the step LFO level changes abruptly at each step (TYPE1: stair-step) or is connected linearly (TYPE2: linear). Values: TYPE1, TYPE2.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep1.label: STEP 1–16 1
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep1.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep2.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep4.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep5.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep6.label: STEP 1–16 6
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep6.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep7.label: STEP 1–16 7
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep7.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep8.label: STEP 1–16 8
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep8.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep9.label: STEP 1–16 9
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep9.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep10.label: STEP 1–16 10
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep10.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep11.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep12.label: STEP 1–16 12
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep12.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep13.label: STEP 1–16 13
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep13.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep14.label: STEP 1–16 14
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep14.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep15.label: STEP 1–16 15
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep15.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep16.label: STEP 1–16 16
fm.pat.tone[1].lfoStep16.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneLevel.label: LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[2].toneLevel.help: Volume of the tone; mainly for adjusting the volume balance between tones. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneCoarseTune.label: TUNE COARSE
fm.pat.tone[2].toneCoarseTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in semitones (±4 octaves). Values: -48–+48.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneFineTune.label: TUNE FINE
fm.pat.tone[2].toneFineTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in 1-cent steps (1/100 semitone). Values: -50–+50.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneRandomPitchDepth.label: RANDOM PITCH
fm.pat.tone[2].toneRandomPitchDepth.help: Width of random pitch deviation each time a key is pressed. Set 0 for no random pitch change. Values: 0–1200 (cents; stored as 31 steps: 0–10, 20–100 by 10, 200–1200 by 100).

fm.pat.tone[2].tonePan.label: PAN
fm.pat.tone[2].tonePan.help: Left/right position of the tone. Values: L64–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[2].tonePanKeyfollow.label: PAN KF (Pan Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].tonePanKeyfollow.help: Makes key position affect panning: positive = notes above C4 pan increasingly to the right; negative = to the left; larger = more change. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneRandomPanDepth.label: RANDOM PAN DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[2].toneRandomPanDepth.help: Stereo position changes randomly each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. Values: 0–63.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneAlternatePanDepth.label: ALT. PAN DEPTH (Alternate Pan Depth)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneAlternatePanDepth.help: Panning alternates between left and right each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. L or R reverses the alternation order: two tones set to L and R respectively alternate opposite to each other. Values: L63–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneEnvMode.label: ENV MODE (Envelope Mode)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneEnvMode.help: With a loop waveform the sound normally continues while the key is held; NO-SUS makes it decay naturally even with the key held. A one-shot wave does not sustain even with SUSTAIN. Values: NO-SUS, SUSTAIN.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneDelayMode.label: TONE DELAY MODE
fm.pat.tone[2].toneDelayMode.help: NORMAL: the tone begins after the delay time. HOLD: begins after the delay time, but if the key is released before the time has elapsed the tone is not played. KEY-OFF-NOR: the tone begins the delay time after the key is released instead of while it is held (e.g. simulating guitar noises). KEY-OFF-DCY: like KEY-OFF-NOR but the TVA envelope already runs while the key is held, so often only the release portion is heard. With a decaying (one-shot) wave, KEY-OFF modes may give no sound. Values: NORMAL, HOLD, KEY-OFF-NOR, KEY-OFF-DCY.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneDelayTime.label: TONE DELAY TIME
fm.pat.tone[2].toneDelayTime.help: Time from key press (or, in KEY-OFF modes, from key release) until the tone sounds. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneDrySendLevel.label: SEND LEVEL OUT (Output Level / TONE OUTPUT LEVEL)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneDrySendLevel.help: Level of the tone's signal sent to the destination set by OUTPUT ASSIGN. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[2].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[2].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneOutputAssign.label: OUTPUT ASSIGN (TONE OUTPUT ASSIGN)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneOutputAssign.help: How the tone's direct sound is output. MFX: stereo through the multi-effect (chorus/reverb can follow). L+R: stereo to the OUTPUT jacks bypassing the MFX. L / R: mono to OUTPUT L / R bypassing the MFX. Valid only if PATCH OUTPUT ASSIGN is TONE. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: MFX, L+R, L, R.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveBender.label: RCV BENDER (Receive Bender)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveBender.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Pitch Bend. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveExpression.label: RCV EXP (Receive Expression)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveExpression.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Expression (CC11). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveHold-1.label: RCV HOLD-1 (Receive Hold-1)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceiveHold-1.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Hold-1 (CC64). No effect if ENV MODE is NO-SUS. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceivePanMode.label: RCV PAN MODE (Receive Pan Mode)
fm.pat.tone[2].toneReceivePanMode.help: How Pan messages are received. CONTINUOUS: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives. KEY-ON: the pan changes only when the next note is played. Pan messages cannot be ignored entirely. Values: CONTINUOUS, KEY-ON.

enumLong.text: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives

fm.pat.tone[2].toneRedamperSwitch.label: REDAMPER
fm.pat.tone[2].toneRedamperSwitch.help: Whether the sound is held when Hold 1 is received after a key is released but before the sound has decayed to silence; set ON to sustain. Effective for piano sounds. Requires RCV HOLD-1 ON. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl1Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-1
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl1Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl1Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl1Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl1Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-2
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-3
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-4
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl2Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-2
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-3
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-4
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl3Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-1
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-3
fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].toneControl4Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveGroupType.label: Wave Group Type
fm.pat.tone[2].waveGroupType.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveGroupID.label: Wave Group ID
fm.pat.tone[2].waveGroupID.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveNumberL.label: WAVE NUMBER L (Mono)
fm.pat.tone[2].waveNumberL.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveNumberR.label: WAVE NUMBER R
fm.pat.tone[2].waveNumberR.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveGain.label: GAIN
fm.pat.tone[2].waveGain.help: Gain (amplification) of the waveform in 6 dB steps; +6 dB doubles the gain. When using the Booster to distort the sound, set this to its maximum. Values: -6, 0, +6, +12 (dB).

fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMSwitch.label: FXM ON
fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMSwitch.help: Whether FXM (frequency cross modulation) is used. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMColor.label: FXM COLOR
fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMColor.help: How FXM performs frequency modulation: higher settings give a grainier sound, lower settings a more metallic sound. Values: 1–4.

fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMDepth.label: FXM DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[2].waveFXMDepth.help: Depth of the modulation produced by FXM. Values: 0–16.

fm.pat.tone[2].wavePitchKeyfollow.label: PITCH KF (Pitch Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].wavePitchKeyfollow.help: Amount of pitch change when you play a key one octave higher. +100: the pitch rises one octave per octave as on a conventional keyboard; +200: two octaves. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (PITCH ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvDepth.help: Depth of the pitch envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -12–+12.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvVelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics control the pitch envelope depth; positive = more effect for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS (T1 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS (T4 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.help: Makes pitch envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position. Relative to C4, positive settings make notes above C4 have increasingly shorter times. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime1.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime2.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime3.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvTime4.help: Pitch envelope times; higher = longer time until the next pitch level is reached. Simplified controls: PITCH ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel0.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel1.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel2.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel3.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[2].pitchEnvLevel4.help: Pitch envelope levels: how the pitch changes at each point relative to the pitch set by COARSE/FINE TUNE. Simplified control PITCH ENV S = L3. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfFilterType.label: FILTER TYPE
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfFilterType.help: OFF: no filter. LPF (low pass): reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound. BPF (band pass): leaves only frequencies around the cutoff; useful for distinctive sounds. HPF (high pass): cuts frequencies below the cutoff; suits percussive sounds emphasizing higher tones. PKG (peaking): emphasizes frequencies around the cutoff; with an LFO sweeping the cutoff gives wah-wah. LPF2: low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF; good for simulated instruments such as acoustic piano. LPF3: low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency; also for acoustic instruments, with a different nuance from LPF2 even with the same envelope. With LPF2/LPF3 the RES setting is ignored. Values: OFF, LPF, BPF, HPF, PKG, LPF2, LPF3.

enumLong.text: reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound
leaves only frequencies around the cutoff
low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF
low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffFrequency.label: CUTOFF (Cutoff Frequency)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffFrequency.help: Frequency at which the filter begins to affect the waveform's frequency components. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.label: CUTOFF KF (Cutoff Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.help: Makes the cutoff depend on the key played. Relative to C4, positive settings raise the cutoff for notes above C4, negative settings lower it; larger = more change. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Cutoff Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the cutoff frequency. FIX: the cutoff is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Cutoff Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.help: How playing velocity changes the cutoff; positive = strongly played notes raise the cutoff (brighter). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfResonance.label: RES (Resonance)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfResonance.help: Emphasizes the region around the cutoff frequency, adding character. Excessively high settings can produce oscillation, causing distortion. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.label: RES VEL SENS (Resonance Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.help: Lets velocity modify the resonance amount; positive = strongly played notes get more resonance. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (FILTER ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvDepth.help: Depth of the TVF envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the TVF envelope. FIX: the envelope is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvVelocitySens.help: How velocity affects the TVF envelope depth; positive = greater effect for strongly played notes, negative = less. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 of the TVF envelope; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 of the TVF envelope; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVF envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime1.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime2.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime3.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvTime4.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel0.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel1.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel2.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel3.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel4.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[2].tvfEnvLevel4.help: TVF envelope levels: how the cutoff changes at each point relative to the CUTOFF value. Simplified FILTER ENV S = L3. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].biasLevel.label: BIAS LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[2].biasLevel.help: Bias makes the volume depend on keyboard position (useful for acoustic instruments). BIAS LEVEL is the angle of the volume change in the selected direction; larger = more change; negative inverts the direction. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].biasPosition.label: BIAS POSITION
fm.pat.tone[2].biasPosition.help: Key relative to which the volume is modified. Values: C-1–G9.

fm.pat.tone[2].biasDirection.label: BIAS DIRECTION
fm.pat.tone[2].biasDirection.help: LOWER: volume modified below the bias position. UPPER: above it. LO&UP: symmetrically on both sides. ALL: volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center. Values: LOWER, UPPER, LO&UP, ALL.

enumLong.text: volume modified below the bias position
volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaLevelVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the volume. FIX: the tone's volume is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaLevelVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaLevelVelocitySens.help: How playing dynamics change the tone's volume; positive = louder the harder you play; negative = softer the harder you play. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1 (attack) of the TVA envelope; positive = faster for strongly played notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 (release); positive = faster for quickly released notes, negative = slower. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVA envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes, negative = longer; larger = more change. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime1.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime2.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime2.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime3.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime3.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime4.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 4
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvTime4.help: TVA envelope times; higher = longer until the next volume level is reached. Simplified AMP ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel1.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel1.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel2.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel2.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel3.label: L1–L3 (Level 1–3) 3
fm.pat.tone[2].tvaEnvLevel3.help: TVA envelope levels: how the volume changes at each point relative to LEVEL. Simplified AMP ENV S = L3 (sustain level). Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoWaveForm[0].label: WAVEFORM 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoWaveForm[0].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRate[0].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRate[0].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoOffset[0].label: OFFSET 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoOffset[0].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRateDetune[0].label: RATE DETUNE 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRateDetune[0].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTime[0].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTime[0].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeMode[0].label: FADE MODE 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeMode[0].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeTime[0].label: FADE TIME 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeTime[0].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoKeyTrigger[0].label: KEY TRIGGER 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoKeyTrigger[0].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPitchDepth[0].label: DEPTH PITCH 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPitchDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvfDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVF 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvfDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvaDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVA 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvaDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPanDepth[0].label: DEPTH PAN 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPanDepth[0].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoWaveForm[1].label: WAVEFORM 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoWaveForm[1].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRate[1].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRate[1].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoOffset[1].label: OFFSET 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoOffset[1].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRateDetune[1].label: RATE DETUNE 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoRateDetune[1].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTime[1].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTime[1].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[1].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeMode[1].label: FADE MODE 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeMode[1].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeTime[1].label: FADE TIME 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoFadeTime[1].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoKeyTrigger[1].label: KEY TRIGGER 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoKeyTrigger[1].help: Whether the LFO cycle restarts in sync with each key press (ON) or free-runs (OFF). Required ON for BEND-UP/BEND-DW waveforms. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPitchDepth[1].label: DEPTH PITCH 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPitchDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects pitch (vibrato). Opposite signs on two tones give opposite modulation phase. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvfDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVF 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvfDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the cutoff frequency (wah). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvaDepth[1].label: DEPTH TVA 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoTvaDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the volume (tremolo). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPanDepth[1].label: DEPTH PAN 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoPanDepth[1].help: How deeply the LFO affects the pan (auto-pan). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStepType.label: STEP TYPE
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStepType.help: Whether the step LFO level changes abruptly at each step (TYPE1: stair-step) or is connected linearly (TYPE2: linear). Values: TYPE1, TYPE2.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep1.label: STEP 1–16 1
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep1.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep2.label: STEP 1–16 2
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep2.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep3.label: STEP 1–16 3
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep3.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep4.label: STEP 1–16 4
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep4.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep5.label: STEP 1–16 5
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep5.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep6.label: STEP 1–16 6
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep6.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep7.label: STEP 1–16 7
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep7.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep8.label: STEP 1–16 8
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep8.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep9.label: STEP 1–16 9
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep9.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep10.label: STEP 1–16 10
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep10.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep11.label: STEP 1–16 11
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep11.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep12.label: STEP 1–16 12
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep12.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep13.label: STEP 1–16 13
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep13.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep14.label: STEP 1–16 14
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep14.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep15.label: STEP 1–16 15
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep15.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep16.label: STEP 1–16 16
fm.pat.tone[2].lfoStep16.help: Step LFO data. With LFO PITCH DEPTH +63, each +1 unit of step data corresponds to +50 cents. Values: -36–+36.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneLevel.label: LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[3].toneLevel.help: Volume of the tone; mainly for adjusting the volume balance between tones. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneCoarseTune.label: TUNE COARSE
fm.pat.tone[3].toneCoarseTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in semitones (±4 octaves). Values: -48–+48.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneFineTune.label: TUNE FINE
fm.pat.tone[3].toneFineTune.help: Pitch of the tone's sound in 1-cent steps (1/100 semitone). Values: -50–+50.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneRandomPitchDepth.label: RANDOM PITCH
fm.pat.tone[3].toneRandomPitchDepth.help: Width of random pitch deviation each time a key is pressed. Set 0 for no random pitch change. Values: 0–1200 (cents; stored as 31 steps: 0–10, 20–100 by 10, 200–1200 by 100).

fm.pat.tone[3].tonePan.label: PAN
fm.pat.tone[3].tonePan.help: Left/right position of the tone. Values: L64–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[3].tonePanKeyfollow.label: PAN KF (Pan Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[3].tonePanKeyfollow.help: Makes key position affect panning: positive = notes above C4 pan increasingly to the right; negative = to the left; larger = more change. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneRandomPanDepth.label: RANDOM PAN DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[3].toneRandomPanDepth.help: Stereo position changes randomly each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. Values: 0–63.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneAlternatePanDepth.label: ALT. PAN DEPTH (Alternate Pan Depth)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneAlternatePanDepth.help: Panning alternates between left and right each time a key is pressed; higher = more change. L or R reverses the alternation order: two tones set to L and R respectively alternate opposite to each other. Values: L63–0–63R.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneEnvMode.label: ENV MODE (Envelope Mode)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneEnvMode.help: With a loop waveform the sound normally continues while the key is held; NO-SUS makes it decay naturally even with the key held. A one-shot wave does not sustain even with SUSTAIN. Values: NO-SUS, SUSTAIN.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneDelayMode.label: TONE DELAY MODE
fm.pat.tone[3].toneDelayMode.help: NORMAL: the tone begins after the delay time. HOLD: begins after the delay time, but if the key is released before the time has elapsed the tone is not played. KEY-OFF-NOR: the tone begins the delay time after the key is released instead of while it is held (e.g. simulating guitar noises). KEY-OFF-DCY: like KEY-OFF-NOR but the TVA envelope already runs while the key is held, so often only the release portion is heard. With a decaying (one-shot) wave, KEY-OFF modes may give no sound. Values: NORMAL, HOLD, KEY-OFF-NOR, KEY-OFF-DCY.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneDelayTime.label: TONE DELAY TIME
fm.pat.tone[3].toneDelayTime.help: Time from key press (or, in KEY-OFF modes, from key release) until the tone sounds. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneDrySendLevel.label: SEND LEVEL OUT (Output Level / TONE OUTPUT LEVEL)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneDrySendLevel.help: Level of the tone's signal sent to the destination set by OUTPUT ASSIGN. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[3].toneChorusSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = MFX
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReverbSendLevelMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone goes through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.label: CHO (Chorus Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[3].toneChorusSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to chorus for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.label: REV (Reverb Send), OUTPUT ASSIGN = non MFX
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReverbSendLevelNonMFX.help: Level sent to reverb for the tone when the tone does not go through the MFX. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneOutputAssign.label: OUTPUT ASSIGN (TONE OUTPUT ASSIGN)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneOutputAssign.help: How the tone's direct sound is output. MFX: stereo through the multi-effect (chorus/reverb can follow). L+R: stereo to the OUTPUT jacks bypassing the MFX. L / R: mono to OUTPUT L / R bypassing the MFX. Valid only if PATCH OUTPUT ASSIGN is TONE. With Structure TYPE 02–10 tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). Values: MFX, L+R, L, R.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveBender.label: RCV BENDER (Receive Bender)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveBender.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Pitch Bend. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveExpression.label: RCV EXP (Receive Expression)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveExpression.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Expression (CC11). Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveHold-1.label: RCV HOLD-1 (Receive Hold-1)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceiveHold-1.help: Whether this tone receives MIDI Hold-1 (CC64). No effect if ENV MODE is NO-SUS. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceivePanMode.label: RCV PAN MODE (Receive Pan Mode)
fm.pat.tone[3].toneReceivePanMode.help: How Pan messages are received. CONTINUOUS: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives. KEY-ON: the pan changes only when the next note is played. Pan messages cannot be ignored entirely. Values: CONTINUOUS, KEY-ON.

enumLong.text: the stereo position changes whenever a Pan message arrives
the pan changes only when the next note is played

fm.pat.tone[3].toneRedamperSwitch.label: REDAMPER
fm.pat.tone[3].toneRedamperSwitch.help: Whether the sound is held when Hold 1 is received after a key is released but before the sound has decayed to silence; set ON to sustain. Effective for piano sounds. Requires RCV HOLD-1 ON. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-1
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-2
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 1-4
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl1Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-2
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 2-4
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl2Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-1
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-2
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-3
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 3-4
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl3Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch1.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-1
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch1.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch2.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-2
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch2.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch3.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-3
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch3.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch4.label: TONE 1–4 (Tone Switch 1–4) 4-4
fm.pat.tone[3].toneControl4Switch4.help: Which tones the matrix control affects. OFF: not applied. ON: applied. REV: applied in reverse. Values: OFF, ON, REV.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveGroupType.label: Wave Group Type
fm.pat.tone[3].waveGroupType.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveGroupID.label: Wave Group ID
fm.pat.tone[3].waveGroupID.help: Which wave bank the wave number refers to. Only INT (internal) exists on the AX-Synth. Values: Type: ---, INT, ---, --- ; ID: OFF, 1–16384.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveNumberL.label: WAVE NUMBER L (Mono)
fm.pat.tone[3].waveNumberL.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveNumberR.label: WAVE NUMBER R
fm.pat.tone[3].waveNumberR.help: Basic waveform of the tone. In mono only L is specified; in stereo R is also specified (select L first, then pick the matching R, whose number is L+1). Values: Off, 1–.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveGain.label: GAIN
fm.pat.tone[3].waveGain.help: Gain (amplification) of the waveform in 6 dB steps; +6 dB doubles the gain. When using the Booster to distort the sound, set this to its maximum. Values: -6, 0, +6, +12 (dB).

fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMSwitch.label: FXM ON
fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMSwitch.help: Whether FXM (frequency cross modulation) is used. Values: OFF, ON.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMColor.label: FXM COLOR
fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMColor.help: How FXM performs frequency modulation: higher settings give a grainier sound, lower settings a more metallic sound. Values: 1–4.

fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMDepth.label: FXM DEPTH
fm.pat.tone[3].waveFXMDepth.help: Depth of the modulation produced by FXM. Values: 0–16.

fm.pat.tone[3].wavePitchKeyfollow.label: PITCH KF (Pitch Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[3].wavePitchKeyfollow.help: Amount of pitch change when you play a key one octave higher. +100: the pitch rises one octave per octave as on a conventional keyboard; +200: two octaves. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (PITCH ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvDepth.help: Depth of the pitch envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -12–+12.

fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvVelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics control the pitch envelope depth; positive = more effect for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS (T1 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvTime1VelocitySens.help: Lets keyboard dynamics affect T1; positive = T1 speeds up for strongly played notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS (T4 Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].pitchEnvTimeKeyFollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfFilterType.label: FILTER TYPE
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfFilterType.help: OFF: no filter. LPF (low pass): reduces all frequencies above the cutoff to round off / un-brighten the sound. BPF (band pass): leaves only frequencies around the cutoff; useful for distinctive sounds. HPF (high pass): cuts frequencies below the cutoff; suits percussive sounds emphasizing higher tones. PKG (peaking): emphasizes frequencies around the cutoff; with an LFO sweeping the cutoff gives wah-wah. LPF2: low pass with half the sensitivity of LPF; good for simulated instruments such as acoustic piano. LPF3: low pass whose sensitivity changes with the cutoff frequency; also for acoustic instruments, with a different nuance from LPF2 even with the same envelope. With LPF2/LPF3 the RES setting is ignored. Values: OFF, LPF, BPF, HPF, PKG, LPF2, LPF3.
