fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffFrequency.label: CUTOFF (Cutoff Frequency)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffFrequency.help: Frequency at which the filter begins to affect the waveform's frequency components. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.label: CUTOFF KF (Cutoff Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffKeyfollow.help: Makes the cutoff depend on the key played. Relative to C4, positive settings raise the cutoff for notes above C4, negative settings lower it; larger = more change. Values: -200–+200.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Cutoff Velocity Curve)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffVelocityCurve.help: Curve by which velocity affects the cutoff frequency. FIX: the cutoff is not affected by velocity. Values: FIX, 1–7.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Cutoff Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfCutoffVelocitySens.help: How playing velocity changes the cutoff; positive = strongly played notes raise the cutoff (brighter). Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfResonance.label: RES (Resonance)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfResonance.help: Emphasizes the region around the cutoff frequency, adding character. Excessively high settings can produce oscillation, causing distortion. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.label: RES VEL SENS (Resonance Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfResonanceVelocitySens.help: Lets velocity modify the resonance amount; positive = strongly played notes get more resonance. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvDepth.label: DEPTH (FILTER ENV DEPTH)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvDepth.help: Depth of the TVF envelope. Higher settings produce greater change; negative settings invert the envelope's shape. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvVelocityCurve.label: VEL CURVE (Velocity Curve)

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvVelocitySens.label: VEL SENS (Velocity Sens)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvVelocitySens.help: How velocity affects the TVF envelope depth; positive = greater effect for strongly played notes, negative = less. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTime1VelocitySens.label: T1 SENS

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.label: T4 SENS
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTime4VelocitySens.help: Lets key release speed affect T4 of the TVF envelope; positive = T4 speeds up for quickly released notes. Values: -63–+63.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.label: TIME KF (Time Keyfollow)
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTimeKeyfollow.help: Makes TVF envelope times T2–T4 depend on key position; relative to C4, positive = shorter times for higher notes. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTime1.label: T1–T4 (Time 1–4) 1
fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvTime1.help: TVF envelope times; higher = longer until the next cutoff level is reached. Simplified FILTER ENV A = T1, D = T3, R = T4. The patch OFFSET ATTACK/RELEASE TIME modifies T1/T4. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvLevel0.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 0

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvLevel1.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 1

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvLevel2.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 2

fm.pat.tone[3].tvfEnvLevel3.label: L0–L4 (Level 0–4) 3

fm.pat.tone[3].biasLevel.label: BIAS LEVEL
fm.pat.tone[3].biasLevel.help: Bias makes the volume depend on keyboard position (useful for acoustic instruments). BIAS LEVEL is the angle of the volume change in the selected direction; larger = more change; negative inverts the direction. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[3].biasPosition.label: BIAS POSITION
fm.pat.tone[3].biasPosition.help: Key relative to which the volume is modified. Values: C-1–G9.

fm.pat.tone[3].biasDirection.label: BIAS DIRECTION
fm.pat.tone[3].biasDirection.help: LOWER: volume modified below the bias position. UPPER: above it. LO&UP: symmetrically on both sides. ALL: volume changes linearly with the bias position at the center. Values: LOWER, UPPER, LO&UP, ALL.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoWaveForm[0].label: WAVEFORM 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoWaveForm[0].help: SIN sine; TRI triangle; SAW-UP sawtooth; SAW-DW sawtooth (negative polarity); SQR square; RND random; BEND-UP: once the attack of the LFO waveform has developed normally, it continues without further change; BEND-DW: once the decay has developed normally, it continues without further change; TRP trapezoid; S&H sample & hold (value changes once per cycle); CHS chaos; VSIN modified sine whose amplitude is randomly varied once each cycle; STEP: waveform generated from LFO STEP 1–16 (stepped change with a fixed pattern, like a step modulator). BEND-UP/BEND-DW require KEY TRIGGER ON, otherwise they have no effect. Values: SIN, TRI, SAW-UP, SAW-DW, SQR, RND, BEND-UP, BEND-DW, TRP, S&H, CHS, VSIN, STEP.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoRate[0].label: RATE (RATE VALUE) 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoRate[0].help: Modulation speed of the LFO. Ignored when WAVEFORM is CHS. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoOffset[0].label: OFFSET 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoOffset[0].help: Raises or lowers the LFO waveform relative to the central value (pitch or cutoff). Positive: modulation occurs upward from the central value. Negative: downward. Values: -100, -50, 0, +50, +100.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoRateDetune[0].label: RATE DETUNE 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoRateDetune[0].help: Subtly changes the LFO rate each time a key is pressed; higher = greater change. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoDelayTime[0].label: DELAY (DELAY TIME) 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoDelayTime[0].help: Time before the LFO effect is applied (or continues) after the key is pressed (or released), depending on FADE MODE. For violin, wind and similar sounds, adding vibrato only after the note has been drawn out can be effective. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].label: DELAY KEYFOLLOW (Delay Time Keyfollow) 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoDelayTimeKeyfollow[0].help: Adjusts DELAY TIME by key position relative to C4; positive = shorter delay for notes above C4. Values: -100–+100.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoFadeMode[0].label: FADE MODE 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoFadeMode[0].help: How the LFO is applied over time (fade in/out after key on/off). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay. Values: ON-IN, ON-OUT, OFF-IN, OFF-OUT.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoFadeTime[0].label: FADE TIME 1
fm.pat.tone[3].lfoFadeTime[0].help: Time over which the LFO amplitude reaches its maximum (or minimum), per FADE MODE. Values: 0–127.

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoKeyTrigger[0].label: KEY TRIGGER 1

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoPitchDepth[0].label: DEPTH PITCH 1

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoTvfDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVF 1

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoTvaDepth[0].label: DEPTH TVA 1

fm.pat.tone[3].lfoPanDepth[0].label: DEPTH PAN 1

sections.title: PATCH COMMON
sections.help: Settings that apply to the whole patch (all four tones).

sections.title: Pitch bend range
sections.help: Range of the TOUCH CONTROLLER ribbon (pitch bend).

sections.title: OFFSET (Modify): patch-wide offsets applied to all tones
sections.help: Offsets that modify the corresponding per-tone parameters of all tones at once. Stored 1–127 with 64 = 0.

sections.title: PORTAMENTO
sections.help: Portamento smoothly changes the pitch from the first-played key to the next-played key.

sections.title: WG (Wave Generator): waveform and pitch
sections.help: Per tone. Modifies waveform, pitch and pitch envelope.

sections.title: TONE DELAY
sections.help: Tone Delay produces a time delay between the key being pressed (or released) and the tone starting to sound; it can shift the timing at which each tone sounds. Unlike an effect delay, the delayed tones can have their own sound and pitch, so arpeggio-like passages can be played with a single key.

sections.title: PITCH ENV (Wave Pitch Envelope)
sections.help: Five levels L0–L4 joined by four times T1–T4; T1 starts at note-on, T4 is the release. Levels are relative to the pitch set by coarse/fine tune.

sections.title: TVF (filter)
sections.help: A filter cuts or boosts a frequency region to change the sound's brightness, thickness or other qualities.

sections.title: FILTER ENV (TVF Envelope) and cutoff velocity
sections.help: Five levels L0–L4 joined by times T1–T4, relative to the CUTOFF value.

sections.title: TVA (amplifier): level, velocity, bias, pan
sections.help: TVA adjusts the volume and stereo position of the tone.

sections.title: AMP ENV (TVA Envelope)
sections.help: Four times T1–T4 and three levels L1–L3 (level 0 at start and end), relative to the LEVEL value.

sections.title: Tone OUTPUT and send levels
sections.help: Where each tone's direct sound goes and how much of it is sent to chorus and reverb. Sounds are always sent to chorus and reverb in mono.

sections.title: LFO1 / LFO2
sections.help: Each tone has two LFOs with identical parameters. They cyclically change pitch (vibrato), cutoff (wah), volume (tremolo) and pan. With Structure TYPE 02–10, tone 1 (3) follows tone 2 (4). ON-IN: apply the LFO gradually after the key is pressed. DELAY TIME = time from key press until the LFO begins; FADE TIME = time for the LFO amplitude to reach maximum after the delay.

sections.title: STEP LFO
sections.help: Data for LFO waveform STEP (one set per tone, shared by LFO1 and LFO2).

sections.title: STRUCTURE (tone pair connection) and BOOSTER
sections.help: TYPE 01: tones 1 and 2 (or 3 and 4) are independent. Use it to preserve PCM sounds or to create and combine sounds per tone.

sections.title: VELOCITY RANGE (TMT)
sections.help: Per tone: which velocities make the tone sound. The force with which keys are played (velocity) and the note number can control which tones sound. For each tone, a velocity range (LOWER/UPPER with FADE LOWER/UPPER) and a key range (LOWER/UPPER with FADE LOWER/UPPER) are set.

sections.title: KEY RANGE (TMT)
sections.help: Per tone: which notes make the tone sound (keyboard split/layer).

sections.title: MATRIX CONTROL 1–4
sections.help: Four matrix controls per patch; each has one SOURCE and up to four DESTINATION/SENS pairs. Matrix Control uses MIDI messages (SOURCE) to change tone parameters (DESTINATION) in real time by an amount (SENS), for chosen tones (TONE). Up to four Matrix Controls per patch; each can control up to four destinations simultaneously.

sections.title: PATCH EFFECTS: ROUTING
sections.help: One MFX, one chorus and one reverb per patch. Patch/tone OUTPUT ASSIGN and the tone send levels (tone.output group) decide what reaches which effect.

sections.title: Multi-effect (MFX) settings
sections.help: Choose a type; its own settings appear below.

sections.title: MFX CONTROL (Multi-Effect Control 1–4)
sections.help: Instead of system exclusive messages, control changes and other common MIDI messages can control the most important MFX parameters in real time (e.g. touch controller -> amount of distortion, keyboard touch -> delay time).

sections.help: Choose a type; its own settings appear below.

sections.title: Reverb unit settings
sections.help: Choose a type; its own settings appear below.

types.name: EQUALIZER
types.description: A four-band stereo equalizer (low, mid x 2, high).

types.name: SPECTRUM
types.description: A stereo spectrum: a type of filter that modifies the timbre by boosting or cutting the level at specific frequencies.

types.name: ISOLATOR
types.description: An equalizer that cuts the volume greatly, allowing you to add a special effect to the sound by cutting the volume in varying ranges.

types.name: LOW BOOST
types.description: Boosts the volume of the lower range, creating powerful lows.

types.name: SUPER FILTER
types.description: A filter with an extremely sharp slope. The cutoff frequency can be varied cyclically.

types.name: STEP FILTER
types.description: A filter whose cutoff frequency can be modulated in steps; you specify the pattern by which the cutoff changes (16-step sequencer; STEP RESET available).

types.name: ENHANCER
types.description: Controls the overtone structure of the high frequencies, adding sparkle and tightness to the sound.

types.name: AUTO WAH
types.description: Cyclically controls a filter to create cyclic change in timbre.

types.name: HUMANIZER
types.description: Adds a vowel character to the sound, making it similar to a human voice (overdrive -> formant filter -> 2-band EQ -> pan).

types.name: SPEAKER SIMULATOR
types.description: Simulates the speaker type and the mic settings used to record the speaker sound.

types.name: PHASER
types.description: A phase-shifted sound is added to the original sound and modulated.

types.name: STEP PHASER
types.description: The phaser effect is varied in steps (stepwise change of the phaser effect at Step Rate).

types.name: MULTI STAGE PHASER
types.description: Extremely high settings of the phase difference produce a deep phaser effect.

types.name: INFINITE PHASER
types.description: A phaser that keeps raising/lowering the frequency at which the sound is modulated.

types.name: RING MODULATOR
types.description: Applies amplitude modulation (AM) to the input signal, producing bell-like sounds. The modulation frequency can also change in response to the volume of the sound sent into the effect.

types.name: STEP RING MODULATOR
types.description: A ring modulator that uses a 16-step sequence to vary the modulation frequency (STEP RESET available).

types.name: TREMOLO
types.description: Cyclically modulates the volume to add tremolo to the sound.

types.name: AUTO PAN
types.description: Cyclically modulates the stereo location of the sound.

types.name: STEP PAN
types.description: Uses a 16-step sequence to vary the panning of the sound (STEP RESET available).

types.name: SLICER
types.description: Applies successive cuts to the sound, turning a conventional sound into one that appears to be played as a backing phrase; especially effective on sustain-type sounds (16-step sequence; STEP RESET available).

types.name: ROTARY
types.description: Simulates the rotary speakers often used with electric organs. The high-range and low-range rotors can be set independently, closely simulating the characteristic modulation. Most suitable for electric organ patches.

types.name: VK ROTARY
types.description: Rotary speaker with modified response and the low end boosted further; same specifications as the VK-7's built-in rotary speaker.

types.name: CHORUS
types.description: A stereo chorus, with a filter to adjust the timbre of the chorus sound.

types.name: FLANGER
types.description: A stereo flanger (LFO in phase for left and right). Produces a metallic resonance that rises and falls like a jet airplane taking off or landing; a filter adjusts the timbre of the flanged sound.

types.name: STEP FLANGER
types.description: A flanger whose pitch changes in steps. The speed of the pitch change can also be specified as a note value of a specified tempo.

types.name: HEXA-CHORUS
types.description: A six-phase chorus (six layers of chorused sound) giving richness and spatial spread.

types.name: TREMOLO CHORUS
types.description: A chorus with added tremolo (cyclic modulation of volume).

types.name: SPACE-D
types.description: A multiple chorus applying two-phase modulation in stereo. It gives no impression of modulation, but a transparent chorus effect.

types.name: 3D CHORUS
types.description: Applies a 3D (RSS) effect to the chorus sound: the chorus sound is positioned 90 degrees left and 90 degrees right.

types.name: 3D FLANGER
types.description: Applies a 3D effect to the flanger sound, positioned 90 degrees left and 90 degrees right.

types.name: 3D STEP FLANGER
types.description: Applies a 3D effect to the step flanger sound, positioned 90 degrees left and 90 degrees right.

types.name: 2BAND CHORUS
types.description: A chorus that applies the effect independently to the low-frequency and high-frequency ranges.

types.name: 2BAND FLANGER
types.description: A flanger that applies the effect independently to the low-frequency and high-frequency ranges.

types.name: 2BAND STEP FLANGER
types.description: A step flanger that applies the effect independently to the low-frequency and high-frequency ranges.

types.name: OVERDRIVE
types.description: Creates a soft distortion similar to that produced by vacuum tube amplifiers (overdrive -> amp simulator -> 2-band EQ).

types.name: DISTORTION
types.description: Produces a more intense distortion than Overdrive. Parameters are the same as 35 OVERDRIVE.

types.name: VS OVERDRIVE
types.description: An overdrive that provides heavy distortion.

types.name: VS DISTORTION
types.description: A distortion that provides heavy distortion. Parameters are the same as 37 VS OVERDRIVE.

types.name: GUITAR AMP SIMULATOR
types.description: Simulates the sound of a guitar amplifier (pre-amp -> speaker).

types.name: COMPRESSOR
types.description: Flattens out high levels and boosts low levels, smoothing out fluctuations in volume.

types.name: LIMITER
types.description: Compresses signals that exceed a specified volume level, preventing distortion.

types.name: GATE
types.description: Cuts the reverb's delay according to the volume of the sound sent into the effect; use it to create an artificial-sounding decrease in the reverb's decay.

types.name: DELAY
types.description: A stereo delay. Feedback Mode NORMAL feeds each channel back into itself; CROSS feeds each channel back into the opposite channel.

types.name: LONG DELAY
types.description: A delay that provides a long delay time.

types.name: SERIAL DELAY
types.description: Two delay units connected in series; feedback can be applied independently to each, producing complex delay sounds.

types.name: MODULATION DELAY
types.description: Adds modulation to the delayed sound (Feedback Mode NORMAL or CROSS as for 43 DELAY).

types.name: 3TAP PAN DELAY
types.description: Produces three delay sounds: center, left and right.

types.name: 4TAP PAN DELAY
types.description: A delay with four delays at fixed stereo locations (shown in the manual's diagram).

types.name: MULTI TAP DELAY
types.description: Four delays whose panning and level can each be set.

types.name: REVERSE DELAY
types.description: Adds a reversed and delayed sound to the input sound; a tap delay is connected immediately after the reverse delay.

types.name: SHUFFLE DELAY
types.description: Adds a shuffle to the delay sound, giving a bouncy delay effect with a swing feel (delays A and B).

types.name: 3D DELAY
types.description: Applies a 3D (RSS) effect to the delay sound, positioned 90 degrees left and 90 degrees right.

types.name: ANALOG DELAY
types.description: A stereo delay whose delay time can be varied smoothly.

types.name: ANALOG LONG DELAY
types.description: A delay whose delay time can be varied smoothly, allowing an extended delay.

types.name: TAPE ECHO
types.description: A virtual tape echo with a realistic tape delay sound; simulates the tape echo section of a Roland RE-201 Space Echo.

types.name: LOFI NOISE
types.description: A lo-fi effect that also adds various types of noise such as white noise and disc (record) noise.

types.name: LOFI COMPRESS
types.description: Intentionally degrades the sound quality for creative purposes (compressor -> lo-fi -> 2-band EQ).

types.name: LOFI RADIO
types.description: A lo-fi effect that also generates radio noise.

types.name: TELEPHONE
types.description: Produces a muffled sound, like that heard through a telephone.

types.name: PHONOGRAPH
types.description: Simulates a sound recorded on an analog record and played back on a record player, including typical record noise and the rotational irregularities of an old turntable.

types.name: PITCH SHIFTER
types.description: A stereo pitch shifter.

types.name: 2VOICE PITCH SHIFTER
types.description: Two pitch shifters that add two pitch-shifted sounds to the original sound.

types.name: STEP PITCH SHIFTER
types.description: A pitch shifter whose amount of pitch shift is varied by a 16-step sequence (STEP RESET available).

types.name: REVERB
types.description: Adds reverberation to the sound, simulating an acoustic space.

types.name: GATED REVERB
types.description: A special reverb in which the reverberant sound is cut off before its natural length.

types.name: OVERDRIVE->CHORUS
types.description: Overdrive followed by chorus, in series.

types.name: OVERDRIVE->FLANGER
types.description: Overdrive followed by flanger, in series.

types.name: OVERDRIVE->DELAY
types.description: Overdrive followed by delay, in series.

types.name: DISTORTION->CHORUS
types.description: Distortion followed by chorus. Parameters as 66 OVERDRIVE→CHORUS with Overdrive Drive/Pan replaced by Distortion Drive/Pan.

types.name: DISTORTION->FLANGER
types.description: Distortion followed by flanger. Parameters as 67 OVERDRIVE→FLANGER with Overdrive Drive/Pan replaced by Distortion Drive/Pan.

types.name: DISTORTION->DELAY
types.description: Distortion followed by delay. Parameters as 68 OVERDRIVE→DELAY with Overdrive Drive/Pan replaced by Distortion Drive/Pan.

types.name: ENHANCER->CHORUS
types.description: Enhancer followed by chorus, in series.

types.name: ENHANCER->FLANGER
types.description: Enhancer followed by flanger, in series.

types.name: ENHANCER->DELAY
types.description: Enhancer followed by delay, in series.

types.name: CHORUS->DELAY
types.description: Chorus followed by delay, in series.

types.name: FLANGER->DELAY
types.description: Flanger followed by delay, in series.

types.name: CHORUS->FLANGER
types.description: Chorus followed by flanger, in series.

types.name: SYMPATHETIC RESONANCE
types.description: On an acoustic piano, holding the damper pedal lets other strings resonate in sympathy with the notes played, creating rich, spacious resonance. This effect simulates these sympathetic resonances (followed by a 3-band EQ).

types.name: CHORUS
types.description: The chorus unit used as a chorus (chorusType = CHORUS).

types.name: DELAY
types.description: The chorus unit used as a stereo delay (chorusType = DELAY) with left, right and center delays.

types.name: REVERB
types.description: Basic reverb unit type (reverbType = REVERB), which also offers delay and pan-delay variations.

types.name: SRV ROOM
types.description: Reverb that simulates typical room acoustic reflections in greater detail.

types.name: SRV HALL
types.description: Reverb that simulates typical concert hall acoustic reflections in greater detail. Same parameters as SRV ROOM.

types.name: SRV PLATE
types.description: Simulates a reverb plate, an artificial reverb unit that derives its sound from the vibration of a metallic plate. Same parameters as SRV ROOM.
